p.i: Materies, ô nox, esto, qua Virginis olim Clausa licèt sacro patuerunt viscera partu, Viscera quæ cœli tempestatúmque potentem Gestauere Deum, tandémque illæsa dedère Humanis cernendum oculis: tu conscia partus Vna nouì, tu nascentis primordia Lucis Luce prior nox vidisti, dignissima Lucis Nomine, non Noctis quæ caca & nigra vocatur: Illius primos Solis quæ senserit ortus, Ipse accepta refert clarus cui lumina Titan, Et quæcunque micant splendenti sydera cælo: Tu teneri primos Sagittus prima puelli, Tu primos cœli plausus, tu gaudia mundi Audisti, nox ô felix, quum læta volantum Ad Domini cunas resonarent agmina fratrum, Et Domino totus nascenti applauderet orbis. Tu vili impositum fœno, stabulóque iacentem Es mirata simul, simul es miserata puellum. Tu quoque pastorum pietatem, & nescia fraudis Pectora mirata es, quum Tityrus inde relictus Accurrens gregibus, CHRISTI natalia lætus Visoret: hinc caderet Damœtas, surgeret Aegò: Dum cœli monitis & claro numinis ore Attoniti, puerum properant inuisere regem. Quid casta matris curas, immixtáque curis Gaudia commemorē? dum tanto pignore, cœli Consortem agnoscit sese, natúmque tuetur In gremio, nasci quem Six dum senserat ipsa, Parturiens, pariensque simul, Virgóq; parensq;

page.notes: Verse text is set in italic with long s and ligatures; the final line is cut off at the page foot and the last word "parensq;" is partly hidden by the catchword "At". "Six" in the line "quem Six dum" is doubtful and may be "Six" or "Sic" [?]. Some ligatures (ct, st) were transcribed as printed; "Tu vili" line uncertain in spelling.
